sections.title: Definition, hallmark and trigger sequence
sections.contentHtml:
Autoimmune hepatitis (AIH) is chronic, unresolving, severe liver inflammation produced by an interaction between environmental triggers, autoantigens and genetic predisposition.

  1. 1
    Genetically predisposed individual
  2. 2
    Exposure to an environmental triggering agent
  3. 3
    Activation of an autoimmune pathogenic process
  4. 4
    Hepatocellular damage, necroinflammation and fibrosis
Histological hallmark

Interface hepatitis with portal plasma-cell infiltration.

  • Most often a chronic hepatitis pattern, but 40% of Type 1 cases may present acutely and mimic toxic or viral hepatitis.
  • Symptoms may include pruritus, anorexia, nausea/vomiting, myalgia, fever, arthritis/arthralgia and amenorrhea.
  • Extrahepatic autoimmune disease may include thyroid disease, ulcerative colitis and less commonly RA, SLE, ITP, pernicious anemia or systemic sclerosis.

sections.title: Treatment indications, regimens and remission
sections.contentHtml:
Prednisone monotherapy

60 mg/day, taper to 30 mg by week 4, then maintenance 20 mg/day until endpoint. Used when combination therapy is unsuitable, including cytopenia, malignancy or pregnancy in the source.

Preferred combination

Prednisone 30 mg/day + azathioprine 50 mg/day; taper prednisolone to 15 mg by week 4, then maintain prednisolone 10 mg/day + azathioprine 50 mg/day.

  • Absolute indications include incapacitating symptoms, relentless progression, AST >10× ULN, AST >5× ULN plus gammaglobulin >2× normal, bridging necrosis or multilobular necrosis.
  • Up to 80% achieve remission.
  • Remission requires disappearance of symptoms; normal bilirubin and IgG; aminotransferases normal or <2× ULN; and normal histology or minimal inflammation without interface hepatitis.
  • Alternative/rescue drugs listed include cyclosporine, 6-MP, ursodeoxycholic acid, budesonide, methotrexate, cyclophosphamide and mycophenolate mofetil.

passages.title: 1. Definition
passages.text:
Autoimmune Hepatitis
Liver Diseases
1. Definition
Autoimmune hepatitis (AIH) is a chronic, unresolving, severe inflammation of the liver resulting from a
complex interaction between triggering environmental factors, autoantigens, and genetic predisposition,
leading to a dysregulated immunoregulatory network.
Defining Characteristics
› Interface hepatitis with portal plasma cell infiltration (hallmark histological finding)
› Hypergammaglobulinemia and presence of circulating autoantibodies
› Continuing / unresolving hepatocellular inflammation and necrosis
› Progressive course — can advance to cirrhosis if untreated
› Diagnosis requires exclusion of other chronic liver diseases (viral, metabolic, drug-induced)

Overlap Syndromes (Variant Forms)
AIH Overlap Syndromes
› AIH + Primary Biliary Cholangitis (PBC)

› 15% of chronic hepatitis C patients have low-titer autoantibodies — ANA titre >1:100 suggests true AIH

5. Clinical Features
The clinical presentation is highly variable — AIH can mimic acute hepatitis, present as chronic liver
disease, or remain completely asymptomatic.
Presentation Patterns
› Chronic hepatitis pattern (most common)
› Acute severe / fulminant hepatitis — history of recurrent bouts
› Asymptomatic in 34% of cases (incidental finding on LFTs)
› May be confused with acute viral hepatitis or toxic hepatitis

8. Liver Transplantation
Indications for Liver Transplant in AIH
› Ascites with hepatic encephalopathy (decompensated cirrhosis)
› Failed glucocorticoid therapy
› Clinical deterioration or worsening while on glucocorticoid therapy
› Hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC)
› MELD score > 15
› Multilobar necrosis with acute liver failure
